paper_details.subjectName: Chemical Properties of Metals and Reactivity Series

questions.text: Quick Revision - Chemical Properties of Metals

definitionBean.title: Chemical Properties of Metals
definitionBean.definition: Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides, react with water to liberate hydrogen gas, and react with dilute acids to give salts and hydrogen.
definitionBean.explanation: Chemically, metals have positively charged ions (tendency to form cations by losing electrons). Their reactivity depends on their activity level.
importantPoints: Reaction with oxygen: Metal $+$ Oxygen $\rightarrow$ Metal oxide (basic)
Reaction with water: Metal $+$ Water $\rightarrow$ Metal oxide/hydroxide $+$ Hydrogen
Reaction with acid: Metal $+$ Dilute acid $\rightarrow$ Salt $+$ Hydrogen gas

definitionBean.title: Reactivity Series
definitionBean.definition: The list arranging metals in order of their decreasing reactivity is called the 'reactivity series'.
definitionBean.explanation: In this series, the most reactive metals are at the top (e.g., Potassium K, Sodium Na) and the least reactive metals are at the bottom (e.g., Gold Au, Silver Ag).
importantPoints: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound
Metals above hydrogen displace hydrogen from dilute acids
Potassium (K) is the most reactive and Platinum (Pt) is the least reactive

questions.text: Subject: Chemical Properties and Extraction of Metals

parts.statement: Explain the reaction of metals with oxygen and water with equations.
parts.correct_answer: Metals combine with oxygen to form oxides and with water to form hydrogen.
parts.explanation: Metals combine with oxygen to form metal oxides (e.g., $2\text{Cu} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CuO}$). Upon reacting with water, some metals form hydrogen gas and hydroxides.

parts.statement: What is the difference between a mineral and an ore? Define metallurgy.
parts.correct_answer: All ores are minerals but all minerals are not ores.
parts.explanation: Naturally occurring elements or compounds in the Earth's crust are called 'minerals'; those minerals from which metals can be extracted profitably and easily are called 'ores'. The process of obtaining pure metals from ores is called 'metallurgy'.
